name: Earth and environment: ClimateBench emissions-to-climate response
description: Learn a compact emissions-response emulator from complete training scenarios and predict source climate anomalies for the entirely withheldSSP245 scenario.

sources.locator: ClimateBench1.0 problem definition, scenario-level split and spatial/global normalized error, Sections2–4.
Official source data/evaluation reference; evaluator and seed independently written.

requirements.datasets: SHA256-locked source bundle E05.json in .cache/science-earth-data. Automatically prepared by scripts/prepare_earth_data.py.

evaluation.benchmark: Earth and environment: ClimateBench emissions-to-climate response
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: fit_climate(training_scenarios,grid) -> model.project_climate(forcing_history) returning declared year x latitude x longitude fields. Input named columns cumulativeCO2,CH4,globalSO2,globalBC. NorESM source climate anomalies, tas inK and precipitation inmm/day. Complete SSP245 withheld; score2080–2100 using cos(latitude)-weighted spatialNRMSE+5*globalNRMSE, then mean variables. Four-variable full leaderboard not claimed for two-variable coarse subset.

provenance.note: Local evaluator, candidate interface and seed recreated from scientific specifications; official benchmark data are reused.

limitations: Source NorESM member means, temperature/precipitation anomalies, area-weighted8×12 spatial adaptation. CompleteSSP245 held out;2080–2100 scored. TrainingSSP370 uses available-member means because two source members end early. Not the full-resolution four-variable leaderboard or observed future climate.
Source data remain local caches with immutable revisions/content hashes and no evaluator network access. Public subsets are development-visible; freeze candidates before wider generalization tests.
Improved source benchmark performance is a scientific-method contribution, not alone a new discovery or operational forecast validation.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Predict spatial climate temperature responses to greenhouse-gas and aerosol emissions.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Resolving regional emissions responses helps understand how different emissions pathways affect future climate.

papers.title: Emulation of the Climate Response to Greenhouse Gas and Aerosol Emissions From High- and Low-Income Nations
papers.primary_goal: Separate and predict spatiotemporal temperature impacts of greenhouse gases and aerosols associated with different emitting regions.
papers.task_relation: The paper solves emissions-to-temperature emulation for CESM2 experiments. The local task instead uses ClimateBench scenarios and a withheld SSP245 response; it tests the same physical response family without reproducing the paper's regional attribution or climate model.

science_relevance.reason: The qualifying paper pursues a climate-response and attribution question. The ClimateBench benchmark paper itself is excluded.
science_relevance.verification_basis: Primary publisher, author, or PubMed/PMC paper abstract and relevant task description inspected on the web; local catalog contract inspected. No independent reproduction of the paper is claimed.

The evidence must explain why the problem matters and how the local task represents it.
